title: Book Three · Chapter 193: Nineteen in May
story:
In May, Ronan turns nineteen.

His fifteen working weeks are over. The April study total is still eight hundred and nineteen and a half. This month's household review has not happened yet.

On his birthday evening, Mum gives him a flat cloth case. She made it from her own cloth, with two pockets inside for letters and route pages.

Ronan opens it carefully. Dad points to the longer pocket.

“The paper can stay flat.”

“Even my very long questions?”

Mum laughs. “Some of them.”

He puts the coastal offer inside and closes the case. It is light enough to hold under one arm.

Kai and Lin arrive while Dad is setting the table. Anna comes a few minutes later with a folded letter for him.

“For later,” she says.

Ronan puts it beside the new case. The others make room around the table. Anna takes his hand under the table.

Dad has brought a small cake from the shop. Mum serves the meal first, and Kai tells them about a customer's very large chair.

“For a very large customer?” Lin asks.

“For a very small dog.”

They all laugh. Kai shows the shape with his hands and explains where the dog likes to sit.

Ronan listens while Mum asks about the cloth on the chair. Dad wants to know how the legs fit. Anna draws the little chair on the edge of a spare page.

Kai points to the little chair. “Beside the window,” he says. “The owner showed me.”

“Did the dog agree?” Ronan asks.

“It was already there.”

“Then the place is right.”

“The old chair was right too. The cloth was not.”

Kai touches the edge of his own seat. “The dog made a hole.”

Lin looks down at the chair beneath Kai.

“Keep your hands still. Mum likes this one.”

Kai puts both hands above the table. Dad passes him a bowl, and he has to lower them again.

Anna laughs so hard that she puts down her pencil. Ronan looks at the small chair on her page. The legs are narrow, but the seat is wide and soft.

“Now it needs a dog,” he says.

“You can draw it.”

He takes the pencil. His first line makes the dog almost as large as the chair.

Kai leans closer.

“That customer will need a new room.”

“Nineteen,” Dad says when the cake is cut.

Ronan looks around the table. There is room for everyone's bowl, though Kai's elbow nearly touches his.

He moves the cake plate into the middle so they can all reach it.

Later, he opens Anna's letter near the kitchen door. The first line asks him to tell her about breakfast in the new city.

He smiles and reads on. She describes an ordinary morning together. Then she asks for stories about his days in the new city.

Anna comes to stand beside him.

“Even breakfast?” he asks.

“Especially breakfast.”

He folds the letter and puts it in the cloth case with his own papers.

Outside, the spring air is mild. Ronan takes her hand. They stand together in the doorway. Behind them, Lin and Kai argue cheerfully about the drawing of the dog's chair.

Mum calls for the last plates. Ronan gives Anna's hand a squeeze, then goes back inside with her to help clear the table.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

cloth case＝布制文件袋；especially＝尤其是；mild＝温和的；squeeze＝轻轻一握。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan何时满十九岁？五月未来的钱已算进八百一十九元五角了吗？
2. 新布袋和Anna的信各有什么实际用途？生日有没有让两人不再去不同城市？

## 读句子

**In May, Ronan turns nineteen.**

拆开看：In May, / Ronan / turns nineteen.

五月／Ronan／满了十九岁。
